claims.text: Local chemical short-range order and the density and distribution of nanoscale structural defects govern the low-field magnetocaloric response and hysteresis of as-deposited non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys.
Rapid solidification produces a high defect density in the as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has a highly ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy undergoes a sharp first-order magnetostructural transition with large hysteresis.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can increase chemical short-range order in the alloy.
Controlled low-temperature annealing can reduce vacancies, dislocations, and incoherent domain boundaries in the hexagonal matrix.
Annealing at approximately 500 °C is below the relevant ordering and recrystallization temperatures for the proposed FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy.
The proposed annealing treatment can evolve short-range order and relax defects without causing substantial grain growth or phase separation.
Annealing-induced atomic reordering minimizes local lattice distortions.
Enhanced short-range order and a refined defect landscape facilitate more uniform magnetic-domain motion.
Enhanced short-range order and reduced defect density lower the energy barriers for the field-induced phase change.
Lower phase-change energy barriers reduce hysteresis during low-applied-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Annealed samples will exhibit a broader and less abrupt magnetostructural transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit lower magnetic hysteresis than the as-deposited baseline under low-field cooling cycles.
Annealing will distribute the magnetic entropy change over a wider temperature range while retaining a sizable magnetocaloric effect.
The predicted behavior applies to non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type alloys produced by similar rapid-deposition methods.
Annealing at excessive temperature may cause grain coarsening or new-phase formation and invalidate the prediction.
Large compositional changes may alter the underlying magnetic interactions and invalidate the prediction.
